entities.summary: John Colet was an English Catholic priest and educational pioneer who played a significant role in the Catholic Reformation in England. He was born in unknown location, but his influence on education and literature is still felt today. Colet's establishment of St Paul's School in London in 1509 marked a turning point in the development of English education, as it emphasized Latin, Greek, and classical studies. This approach would later become a model for British public schools and influenced the curriculum for centuries to come. As a writer and scholar, Colet produced several works on biblical interpretation and Christian theology, which were widely read and studied during his lifetime. One notable example is 'In Praise of Chaucer,' published in 1504, which helped establish Geoffrey Chaucer as the father of English literature. Colet's legacy can be seen in the many schools and universities he founded or supported, including St Paul's School, Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge University. His emphasis on classical education and biblical studies paved the way for future generations of scholars and thinkers. The English Reformation and the rise of Protestantism had a profound impact on Colet's life and work, as he struggled to balance his Catholic faith with his commitment to reforming the Church of England. Despite facing persecution and controversy, Colet remained steadfast in his beliefs and continued to produce influential works until his death in 1519. His story serves as a testament to the power of conviction and the enduring impact of educational innovation.
